page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores across an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and BMI2. It is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle dedicated GPUs or local storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent disk access, and includes a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.g6.8xlarge predominantly in the middle tier of performance. In computational testing, multi-threaded stress-ng (28006.29) and multi-core Geekbench (10179.0) scores align with middle 50% benchmarks, whereas single-core stress-ng (1311.98) and single-threaded gzip compression place in the bottom 25%. Memory throughput remains stable, recording 108.04 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 47.67 GB/sec for writes. PassMark tests confirm consistent mid-range capacity across generic CPU tasks (27100.23), cryptographic operations (12932.22), and database benchmarks (10887.59). Network throughput supports static web serving at 20.21 GB/sec alongside 26.79 million Redis SET operations per second.

The instance delivers balanced compute density and standard resource distribution without the hardware overhead of attached NVMe disks or accelerators. The tradeoff lies in modest single-thread execution speed, meaning it is less optimal for strictly serial tasks. The configuration is best aligned with multi-threaded, memory-balanced workloads such as web serving pools, middle-tier enterprise backends, container orchestration nodes, Redis in-memory caches, and multi-tenant application deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on KVM. Maintaining a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, the instance incorporates 16 physical cores, AVX-512 vector support, and a 10 Gbps baseline network capacity. It includes zero bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage for volume persistence. Performance across Geekbench, PassMark, and multi-core stress-ng tests places firmly in the mid-range distribution, though single-core throughput exhibits lower relative velocity. Memory bandwidth yields 108.04 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 47.67 GB/sec for writes, sustaining 26.79 million Redis SET operations per second. This profile serves standard enterprise backends, distributed microservices, application servers, and Redis caching environments requiring balanced CPU and memory allocation without specialized local disk IOPS requirements.
